gen-dafont-woodgod-gf-noto-sans-khmer: Heavy vintage swagger, then a quiet turn. Woodgod stamps its tall lowercase almost up to the capitals, and Noto Sans Khmer, a plain sans, keeps its openings generous enough to read for pages without tiring.
gen-dafont-woodgod-gf-noto-sans-khojki: Woodgod's lowercase nearly climbs to capital height. Noto Sans Khojki gives the pair its strength, with wide exits and a large, clear eye on every e that let light straight through the text.
gen-dafont-woodgod-gf-noto-sans-khudawad: Chunky, vintage and loud about it. Woodgod is best at commanding attention with its channeled bowls, while Noto Sans Khudawadi, a plain sans, is best at staying approachable, its rounds left unlatched.
gen-dafont-woodgod-gf-noto-sans-kr: Commanding from the first letter, Woodgod pushes its tall lowercase close to the capitals, with a wide channel cut into every bowl. And Noto Sans KR holds the other side, with generous curve gaps and stubby ascenders beside a big x-height.
gen-dafont-woodgod-gf-noto-sans-lao: Noto Sans Lao lifts its x-height well above the usual and keeps its mouths open on c, e and a. Noto Sans Lao against Woodgod is a lively match, since both lean on tall lowercase, one vintage and loud, one modern.
gen-dafont-woodgod-gf-noto-sans-lao-loop: A wide channel runs into every bowl of Woodgod's tall, vintage lowercase, which crowds right up against the capitals. Noto Sans Lao Looped, a plain sans, answers by setting words as solid blocks.
gen-dafont-woodgod-gf-noto-sans-lepcha: Approachable and sturdy, this body keeps its curves wide open, with a lowercase that has the stature of cast iron capitals. Noto Sans Lepcha supplies the sans calm while Woodgod brings its commanding, vintage voice, and their tall letters line up nicely.
gen-dafont-woodgod-gf-noto-sans-limbu: Approachable curves gape wide in the tall-bodied small letters of Noto Sans Limbu, a contemporary sans-serif. Woodgod's vintage swagger sits above it comfortably.
gen-dafont-woodgod-gf-noto-sans-lydian: Noto Sans Lydian keeps its capitals barely taller than lowercase, with an opening as wide as a sprung paper clip. But the pair's real strength is how Woodgod's commanding, vintage heading meets that gentle sans.
gen-dafont-woodgod-gf-noto-sans-mahajani: Woodgod carries a commanding, vintage weight up top. Its strongest quality is the shared tall lowercase, which Noto Sans Mahajani, a plain sans, echoes with a wide funnel-like throat in the e.
